item.title: 39 days to election: Orbán warns of a possible Ukrainian attack but rules out postponing election
item.description: In our regular digest of the week’s news from the Hungarian campaign trail: opinion polls, why Hungarian PM Orbán does not rule out deploying soldiers on the streets, claims Ukraine is financing the opposition Tisza party, and Tisza mobilises in the countryside.

item.title: EU and Gulf states urge Iran to halt attacks amid escalation risks
item.description: Asked if southern EU states were at risk of further aggression, EU commissioner Dubravka Šuica said: "It's not easy to anticipate at this moment, but I don't think it will happen".

item.title: The secret European Commission group driving EU deportations
item.description: First launched in late 2022, the so-called High Level Network for Returns (HLNR) used the October 7 Hamas terror attack on Israel as a justification to enforce the exchange of data of individuals with a deportation order and flagged as “potential terrorists”.

item.title: Listen: Does Spanish PM Sánchez have real EU backing in his standoff with Trump?
item.description: A transatlantic rift is opening. Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez has condemned the US-Israeli attacks on Iran and blocked American access to Spanish bases —directly challenging Donald Trump. The question now: how far can Spain go in defying Washington?

item.title: Europe still in shadow of post-WWI imperial collapse
item.description: Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine shows how the continent has not yet solved the problem of what order comes after imperial collapse

item.title: Cocoa price slumps, despite EU deforestation law
item.description: Cocoa prices have collapsed, defying expectations that EU due diligence requirements would push up the cost of cocoa and chocolate.

item.title: EU and Canada eye digital trade deal, in wake of US hostility
item.description: The commissioned announced Friday, that the EU and Canada have begun to negotiate a so-called ‘Digital Trade Agreement’, with the aim of boosting legal certainty and fair digital trade across the Atlantic.

item.title: Is Europe succeeding in combatting violence against women?
item.description: Despite changes in both national and EU laws, and years of public awareness campaigns, violence against women is still a serious problem across Europe. In some countries, it is even getting worse. A new EU law has been adopted, with full implementation in 2027. So how are different national governments trying to deal with the problem?

item.title: Iran threatens ‘targets’ in Europe, as EU warships flock to Cyprus
item.description: "If any [European] country joins in the aggression against Iran ... they will be also the legitimate targets for Iranian retaliation," Iran's deputy foreign minister warned on French TV.

item.title: THIS WEEK: MEPs vote on deportation bill, as Iran war keeps Europe on edge
item.description: MEPs prepare to vote on a controversial deportation bill while debates intensify over Europe’s security amid the Iran war. Armenia’s prime minister addresses parliament, ministers tackle labour shortages and EU finances, and tensions rise over Ukraine funding as Hungary threatens a veto ahead of next week’s EU summit.
